title: Bloom's Taxonomy and the Grammar of Learning Objectives (1956)
explainer: Benjamin Bloom and a committee of examiners published a classification of educational goals in 1956, ranking cognitive skills from recalling facts up through analysis, synthesis, and evaluation, originally meant to help write better exam questions. It is now the default vocabulary curriculum designers use to decide what a lesson is actually trying to build in a learner - recall versus application versus critique - which is exactly the design problem this lesson is about.

title: Cognitive Load Theory and Why Curricula Shouldn't Overwhelm Working Memory (1988)
explainer: Studying how people solve problems, John Sweller found that open-ended problem-solving strategies like means-ends analysis consume working memory that could otherwise go toward building durable mental schemas, and he formalized this in a 1988 paper as cognitive load theory. It gives curriculum designers a concrete, evidence-based reason to sequence material, worked examples, and practice deliberately rather than just presenting content and expecting it to stick.
